children: , the consumer-technology and digital-services giant, released Siri AI through its newest operating-system updates Monday, finally pushing its long-awaited AI assistant from promise into users' hands. Shares slipped roughly 1% to $329.76 Tuesday afternoon as investors weighed whether the beta rollout is enough to narrow Apple's perceived AI gap. The valuation picture is already demanding: the shares trade 15.51% above the $285.49 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors are paying for meaningful execution rather than another incremental software upgrade.

The new assistant is rolling out in English across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and visionOS 27 on devices supporting Apple Intelligence. More languages are scheduled for October, but the launch still excludes iPhones in the European Union at the outset. Apple's support page also warns that some users may encounter a waitlist before downloading the software. That makes this less of a finished-product moment and more of a live test of whether Apple can turn its enormous installed base into an AI distribution advantage.

The financial stakes are substantial. Apple generated $109.4 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, with roughly $54.3 billion coming from the iPhone alone. Nearly half of quarterly sales therefore sit inside the product ecosystem most capable of benefiting from a smarter, stickier Siri. Apple has now cleared the first hurdle by shipping the technology. The harder question is whether adoption, reliability and international expansion can make Siri AI financially visible enough to justify a stock already trading well above its GF Value estimate.

title: Apple Falls as Siri AI Arrives Behind a Beta Label
